scenarios.name: single filer, Massachusetts state contributory pension: fully exempt under MA law, engine taxes it in full
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts', section 'Massachusetts state and local employee contributory pension': 'Massachusetts state/local employee pensions are contributory annuity, pension, endowment, or retirement funds of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (or any of its political subdivisions)...Distributions made to you from a Massachusetts state and local employee contributory plan are excluded from Massachusetts gross income even though they are included in federal gross income.' No age gate is stated for this exclusion. LABEL STILL WRONG, RE-LABEL IN TASK 4: this row reads 'otherStateOrLocal' only because the PlanSource enum had no case for the taxpayer's OWN state system when this fixture was written. Phase 5b Task 1 ADDED that case, 'ownStateOrLocal', which is what a Commonwealth of Massachusetts contributory pension is to a Massachusetts resident. Task 2 re-labelled Kansas's KPERS rows onto it and deliberately left Massachusetts's to Task 4, so the change lands together with Massachusetts's rule and the out-of-state guard case that rule needs, exactly as Kansas did. This is the SAME mislabel Kansas carried: 'otherStateOrLocal' means a DIFFERENT state's system, and its entire reason for existing is to stop an out-of-state pension claiming a state's own exclusion, so a Massachusetts rule naming it would exempt a California public pension held by a Massachusetts resident. Re-label MA-1 and MA-3 to 'ownStateOrLocal' and ADD an out-of-state guard case before writing the rule. Arithmetic: $60,000 fully excluded, $0 state taxable income (MA's stateDeduction is 'none' in this app's config, so there is no separate standard deduction to apply), tax = $0.00.

knownDefect.summary: MA state/local contributory pensions are fully excluded from MA gross income; statetax-2026-MA.json has no perSourceExemptions, so the engine pools it into ordinary taxable income and taxes it at the flat 5% rate.

scenarios.name: single filer, noncontributory municipal pension: correctly fully taxable, no MA exclusion applies -- contrast/regression case
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts' enumerates a closed list of exempt pension categories (MA/local contributory, federal contributory, MBTA, out-of-state reciprocal contributory, railroad retirement, U.S. uniformed-services noncontributory). A noncontributory municipal pension -- one where the employee made no contributions, distinct from the U.S. uniformed-services noncontributory exemption which is scoped specifically to military service -- appears on none of those lists, so by the closed-list structure of this guidance it remains ordinary taxable pension income under M.G.L. c. 62 (this is an inference from the enumeration's closed-list structure, not a sentence stating 'noncontributory municipal pensions are taxable' verbatim on the page). Arithmetic: $60,000 fully taxable at the flat 5% rate = $3,000.00.

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses have MA state/local contributory pensions: fully exempt under MA law, engine taxes the full household income
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts', section 'Massachusetts state and local employee contributory pension' (see single-filer case above for the exact quote). No per-taxpayer cap is stated -- distributions are excluded outright regardless of amount. LABEL STILL WRONG, RE-LABEL IN TASK 4: both rows here read 'otherStateOrLocal' for what are Commonwealth of Massachusetts systems, i.e. the taxpayer's OWN state. See the single-filer case above for why that label is dangerous rather than merely imprecise, and for the instruction to re-label to 'ownStateOrLocal' (added by Phase 5b Task 1) and add an out-of-state guard case. Arithmetic: $40,000 + $35,000 = $75,000, all fully excluded, $0 state taxable income, tax = $0.00.

knownDefect.summary: Both spouses' MA contributory pensions should be fully excluded; the engine's empty perSourceExemptions for MA excludes neither, taxing the full $75,000 household income at 5%.

scenarios.name: MFJ, one spouse's U.S. uniformed-services pension is exempt and the other spouse's private 401(k) distribution is not: one spouse qualifies
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts', section 'U.S. military non-contributory pension': 'U.S. military pensions, which are included in federal gross income, are excluded from Massachusetts gross income.' LABEL STILL WRONG, RE-LABEL IN TASK 4: this row reads 'federalCivilian' only because the PlanSource enum had no distinct case for U.S. uniformed-services retired pay when this fixture was written. Phase 5b Task 1 ADDED that case, 'uniformedServices'. Task 2 re-labelled Vermont's military rows onto it and deliberately left Massachusetts's to Task 4, so the change lands together with Massachusetts's rule and its own guard cases. Do NOT write the military exclusion against 'federalCivilian': mass.gov's guidance exempts U.S. military pensions, and separately treats federal CIVILIAN (CSRS/FERS) pensions under a different heading, so a rule naming 'federalCivilian' would over-exempt. Re-label this row to 'uniformedServices' first. The private 401(k) distribution is ordinary taxable pension/annuity income with no MA exclusion. Arithmetic: $30,000 military fully excluded; $30,000 private taxable; $30,000 x 5% = $1,500.00.

knownDefect.summary: The military spouse's pension should be fully excluded while the private 401(k) spouse's distribution stays taxable; the engine excludes neither (no perSourceExemptions for MA), taxing the full $60,000.
